intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Tour
experiences.description: Witness the breathtaking sunrise over the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex, one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs, towering spires, and ancient Khmer architecture with a knowledgeable local guide who brings the history of the Khmer Empire to life.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Sanloem Beach Snorkeling & Island Hopping
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring the crystal-clear turquoise waters and pristine white sand beaches of Koh Rong Sanloem. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, hop between secluded coves, and relax on some of Southeast Asia's most unspoiled beachfront shores.

experiences.name: Sihanoukville Beachfront Khmer Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class held steps from the beach in Sihanoukville. Learn to prepare traditional Cambodian dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and fresh mango salad using locally sourced ingredients. Includes a guided visit to a local market to select fresh produce before cooking.

experiences.name: Kampot Riverside Cultural & Pepper Farm Tour
experiences.description: Explore the charming French colonial town of Kampot along its scenic riverside, then venture into the lush countryside to visit a world-famous Kampot pepper farm. Learn about the history and cultivation of one of Cambodia's most prized exports while tasting fresh green, red, and black peppercorns.

experiences.name: Kep Crab Market Sunset Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Visit the legendary Kep Crab Market at golden hour, where local fisherwomen sell the freshest blue swimming crabs straight from the Gulf of Thailand. Enjoy a beachfront seafood feast of grilled crab with Kampot pepper sauce, grilled prawns, and fresh fish while watching the sun dip below the horizon over the sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay in the Angkor Archaeological Park area (negotiate fare, expect $5–8 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the guesthouse neighborhood to orient yourself.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in Siem Reap town center (~15 min tuk-tuk). Browse the night market stalls, soak in the lively atmosphere, and enjoy your first taste of Cambodian street food. Watch a free Apsara dance preview often performed outside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) from a local stall near the airport or guesthouse for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — try amok (fish curry in coconut) and jasmine rice for ~$4–6 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD at the airport (Cambodia widely accepts USD). Tuk-tuks are the best budget transport. Negotiate all fares upfront. SIM cards available at the airport for ~$3–5 USD with data.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn and hire a tuk-tuk driver for a full-day Angkor pass (~$37 USD for 1 day or $62 for 3 days — opt for 3-day if you plan multiple visits). Arrive at Angkor Wat before sunrise (~5:30 AM) to witness the iconic sunrise reflection over the main temple. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex: enter through the South Gate with its towering stone faces, visit the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take a short break with a coconut water from a local vendor (~$1 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse to rest and cool down. Head back to Siem Reap town for dinner and explore the Angkor Night Market for affordable souvenirs — silk scarves, carvings, and handicrafts starting at $2–3 USD.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — pack a banana or snack from a market stall near the temple entrance (~$0.50 USD). Many vendors sell baguettes and coffee outside Angkor Wat gates.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the open-air local restaurants inside the Angkor complex near Angkor Thom — rice with grilled pork or vegetables for ~$3–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Try Chamkar Vegetarian Restaurant in Siem Reap for a hearty plant-based Khmer meal for ~$4–5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 2 liters of water. Temples require covered shoulders and knees. A full-day tuk-tuk hire costs ~$15–20 USD — negotiate the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3-day Angkor pass to visit the 'jungle temples.' Start with Ta Prohm — the atmospheric temple famously overgrown with giant tree roots, used as a filming location for Tomb Raider. Arrive early (~7:30 AM) before tour groups. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a quieter, less-crowded Buddhist monastery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Pre Rup, a 10th-century state temple with panoramic views from its upper tiers — great for photos. Then visit the East Mebon temple on a former artificial island. Cool off with a swim at your guesthouse pool (if available) or relax with a $3 traditional Khmer massage at a local training school.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the vibrant Siem Reap Night Market along the river. Watch local artisans at work and support fair-trade craft shops. Enjoy a cold Angkor beer (~$1 USD) at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a local bakery — Cambodian baguette with pâté or eggs for ~$1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Roadside BBQ stall near Ta Prohm — grilled corn, skewers, and rice for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth. Excellent Khmer cuisine for ~$5–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets very crowded midday — arrive early. Bring insect repellent for the jungle temples. Stay hydrated in the November heat (~28–32°C).

day_by_day.morning: Use the 3rd day of your Angkor pass. Visit the remote and stunning Banteay Srei temple (~35 km north of Siem Reap), known for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the 'jewel of Khmer art.' Hire a tuk-tuk for the round trip (~$15–18 USD). Stop at the Landmine Museum on the way to learn about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Siem Reap and stop at the Cambodian Cultural Village for a budget-friendly overview of Cambodian ethnic traditions, architecture, and dance performances (~$9 USD entry). Alternatively, visit the free Wat Bo pagoda in town to see well-preserved 19th-century murals.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Kandal Village boutique district for window shopping, then settle in for a cooking class or simply enjoy a sunset drink along the Siem Reap River promenade.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local market stall — rice porridge (bobor) with ginger and pork for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the market for the Banteay Srei trip or eat at a local village restaurant near the temple for ~$3 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Market — lok lak (stir-fried beef), fried rice, and fresh spring rolls for ~$3–5 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a must-see but requires early departure. Confirm tuk-tuk pickup time the evening before. The Landmine Museum is donation-based and deeply moving — recommended for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Depart from Chong Kneas floating village (~15 min from Siem Reap). Witness the extraordinary floating villages, schools, and churches of the ethnic Vietnamese and Khmer communities. Boat tours cost ~$10–15 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop in Siem Reap town (free entry) to see skilled artisans crafting traditional silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings — a living cultural heritage experience. Browse the fair-trade shop for affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Smile of Angkor or Koulen II Restaurant — tickets ~$12–15 USD including dinner buffet, making it a cost-effective cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Blue Pumpkin Café — smoothie bowl and toast for ~$3–4 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat near the Tonlé Sap dock — grilled fish with rice from a lakeside stall for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Included in the Apsara dinner show (~$12–15 USD) — Khmer buffet with rice, curries, and desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Water levels on Tonlé Sap are high in November (post-monsoon), making it an ideal time to visit the floating villages. Bargain respectfully at the lake — avoid pushy souvenir sellers on boats. Bring small USD bills.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a budget bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~6 hours, $7–10 USD via Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — book ahead). Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh (~1:00–2:00 PM). Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (dorms from $5, private rooms from $12–15 USD). Take a walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade, visit the Royal Palace exterior, and admire the Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the lively riverfront area, browse street stalls, and visit the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) if still open for local goods and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at guesthouse or a Siem Reap café before bus departure — bread, eggs, and coffee for ~$2 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a rest stop along the highway — local rice dish for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — fish amok or beef lok lak for ~$4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets at least a day in advance during peak season. Giant Ibis is slightly pricier (~$12) but more reliable and comfortable. Store valuables securely on the bus. Phnom Penh is more urban — stay alert in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention center. A deeply sobering and essential historical experience (~$3 USD entry + optional $6 audio guide). Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$10 round trip) to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields), ~15 km from the city center ($3 USD entry). The memorial stupa and audio guide provide powerful insight into Cambodia's tragic 1970s history. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia (~$10 USD) for Khmer art and history exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the FCC (Foreign Correspondents' Club) area for sunset drinks over the Mekong River. Walk along the riverfront and enjoy the evening breeze. Visit the Night Market near the riverside for local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Local breakfast at a Phnom Penh café — rice soup or fried noodles for ~$1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tuol Sleng at a local restaurant — bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) for ~$2 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise supporting street youth. Tapas-style Khmer food for ~$5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and S-21 are emotionally intense — take your time and be respectful. Not recommended for very young children. Carry water and take breaks. These sites are among the most important historical landmarks in Southeast Asia.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, $7–9 USD) or opt for the more scenic Kampot route (~3 hours, $6–8 USD). For beach lovers, head to Koh Rong Sanloem island via Sihanoukville ferry (~$25 USD round trip ferry + $8–12 budget bungalow). Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Sanloem or Otres Beach (Sihanoukville). Check into a budget beach bungalow. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine white sand beach, swimming in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Enjoy bioluminescent plankton in the water after dark (November is a good month for this phenomenon). Relax at a beachside bar with a $1–2 local beer.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the bus — baguette and coffee from a Phnom Penh street stall for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a rest stop or pack snacks for the journey.
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled seafood at a beachside shack — grilled fish, squid, and rice for ~$5–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rong Sanloem is quieter and more budget-friendly than Koh Rong. November weather on the coast can occasionally bring rain showers but is generally pleasant. Bring cash — ATMs are limited on the islands. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day. Wake up early for a peaceful sunrise walk along the deserted beach. Rent a snorkel set (~$3–5 USD/day) and explore the coral reefs just offshore. The water visibility in November is excellent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget island-hopping boat tour (~$10–15 USD) to explore nearby beaches, hidden lagoons, and snorkeling spots. Alternatively, hike through the jungle interior of the island to a secluded beach on the other side (~1.5 hours each way, free).
day_by_day.evening: Final beach evening — enjoy a bonfire on the beach (check if permitted), stargaze in the clear night sky away from city light pollution, and reflect on the journey. Try a fresh coconut cocktail (~$3 USD).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or beachside café — eggs, toast, and fresh fruit for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — buy fresh fruit, bread, and snacks from a small island shop for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: BBQ dinner at a beachside restaurant — whole grilled snapper with vegetables and rice for ~$6–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen regularly — beach days can be deceptively intense under the Cambodian sun. Respect the marine environment — do not touch or stand on coral. Keep the beach clean.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take one last swim or sunrise walk on the beach. Pack up and check out of your bungalow. Take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville mainland. Depending on your departure flight, either head directly to Phnom Penh International Airport (~4 hours by bus, $8–10 USD) or spend a few hours in Sihanoukville.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, visit Otres Market in Sihanoukville for last-minute souvenirs — handmade jewelry, krama scarves, and local crafts at affordable prices. Alternatively, relax at Otres Beach for a final hour of sunshine before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, rich history, vibrant culture, and stunning beaches. Reflect on the incredible value and depth of experience this budget trip has provided.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — rice porridge or fried rice with egg at a local stall for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Sihanoukville bus station or a roadside restaurant — Khmer noodles or fried rice for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or snacks for the journey home — budget $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 4–5 hours of travel time from Sihanoukville/Koh Rong to Phnom Penh Airport. Book your return bus in advance. Keep $25 USD cash for airport departure tax if not included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it — verify). Total estimated budget for 10 days: $250–350 USD excluding flights, covering accommodation, transport, food, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and rest after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the hotel neighborhood. Visit the nearby Angkor Wat outer walls and reflection pond for a first stunning glimpse of the temple at golden hour. Pick up a multi-day Angkor Pass from the official ticket office (3-day or 7-day pass recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area in Siem Reap town for a lively introduction to local nightlife and street food culture. Explore the night market stalls selling silk scarves, handicrafts, and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a local café near the hotel — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) for around $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant — authentic Khmer cuisine, mid-range pricing ($10–20 per person). Try Amok fish curry and Lok Lak beef.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local exchange booth (USD is widely accepted in Cambodia). Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area cost roughly $8–12. Stay hydrated — November is warm but manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for sunrise at Angkor Wat (depart hotel by 5:15 AM). Watch the sun rise over the iconic five towers reflected in the western pond — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue inside Angkor Wat to the upper levels and inner sanctum. After lunch, visit the nearby Angkor Thom complex — enter through the South Gate lined with stone gods and demons, then explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Baphuon Temple and Phimeanakas within Angkor Thom, then watch sunset from the Terrace of the Elephants. Return to Siem Reap town for dinner and a traditional Apsara dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a roadside stall near Angkor Wat ($2–4)
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the open-air restaurants near Angkor Thom — try a fresh spring roll plate and coconut water ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara dance show at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor — set menu dinner with cultural performance ($20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temple sanctuaries. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the full day (approx. $15–20) — many speak English.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the iconic 'Tomb Raider temple' where massive silk-cotton tree roots dramatically engulf ancient stone walls. Explore the atmospheric corridors and moss-covered galleries. Then head to Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist temple with beautiful devata carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Srah Srang, a royal bathing pool with a beautiful lakeside terrace — perfect for a peaceful rest. Then explore Pre Rup, a 10th-century temple mountain with panoramic views from the top, especially lovely in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a deep dive into Khmer history, art, and the civilization that built Angkor. The museum is air-conditioned and beautifully curated ($12 entry fee). Afterward, stroll along the Siem Reap River promenade.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café — try Khmer rice porridge (Bobor) with ginger and egg ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Srah Srang — grab fresh fruit, sandwiches, or snacks from a local vendor ($4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine in a garden setting, featuring refined traditional dishes ($15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded mid-morning — arrive early. The Angkor National Museum closes at 6:30 PM. November evenings are pleasant for riverside walks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day excursion to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. Famous for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, this 10th-century temple is considered the jewel of Khmer art. Arrive early before tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at Kbal Spean — the 'River of a Thousand Lingas' — a sacred riverbed carved with Hindu iconography set in a forested hillside. A 30-minute jungle hike leads to the carvings and a small waterfall. Also visit the nearby Banteay Samré temple.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique shop — watch skilled artisans carve stone, lacquer wood, and weave silk in the tradition of ancient Khmer craftspeople. Browse fair-trade products. End the evening with a relaxing dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before the early departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in the Banteay Srei village area — simple Khmer set meal with rice, vegetables, and grilled fish ($6–9)
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Sugar Palm — beloved Siem Reap restaurant known for traditional Khmer recipes passed down through generations ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk or private driver for the Banteay Srei day trip ($25–35 for the full day). Kbal Spean requires moderate fitness for the jungle trail — wear good shoes. Bring insect repellent for the forest walk.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the floating villages on Tonlé Sap Lake — take a boat tour from Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk village. Witness the extraordinary life of communities living on stilted houses and floating platforms on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. The lake is at high water in November, creating a magical flooded forest landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit Wat Bo Pagoda — one of the oldest temples in the city, with beautifully preserved 19th-century murals depicting scenes from the Ramayana. Then explore the charming French colonial quarter near the river.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free meditation or yoga session offered by some boutique hotels and wellness centers near Angkor. Afterward, explore the Kandal Village neighborhood — Siem Reap's boutique district with independent cafés, galleries, and concept stores.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fuel up before the boat trip
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — grilled fish with rice and local greens ($7–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Jomno Restaurant or a street food tour with a local guide — sample num banh chok (Khmer noodles), grilled skewers, and fresh mango sticky rice ($10–15 total)

day_by_day.notes: The Tonlé Sap boat tour costs approximately $15–20 per person. Kampong Phluk is more scenic than Chong Kneas but requires a longer journey. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride. Responsible tourism tip: choose community-based tour operators.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: early morning departure from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh by express bus or domestic flight (bus: ~6 hours, $10–15; flight: ~45 min, $50–80). If taking the bus, enjoy the scenic Cambodian countryside along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel near the riverfront. After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of gilded spires, sacred Buddha statues, and 5,000 silver floor tiles ($10 entry). Dress modestly.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverfront promenade as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse the lively riverside bars, cafés, and restaurants. Visit the night market (Phsar Reatrey) for local street food and handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a café before departure from Siem Reap
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus (packed snacks) or at a roadside restaurant stop — rice with pork or chicken ($4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant in Phnom Penh — a celebrated social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a colonial villa ($15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus or flight ticket in advance. Giant Ibis and Mekong Express are reliable bus operators. Store valuables securely on the bus. Phnom Penh is more urban and traffic-heavy than Siem Reap — use Grab app for safe and affordable rides.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and important historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge regime's atrocities from 1975–1979. Allow 2–3 hours and consider hiring an audio guide or survivor guide for context. This is emotionally heavy but essential for understanding Cambodia's history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located 15 km outside the city center. The memorial includes a Buddhist stupa filled with victims' skulls and an excellent audio guide narrated by survivors. Return to the city and visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, surrounded by a peaceful park.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts ($10 entry, closes at 5 PM). Afterward, enjoy sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong River.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café — French-influenced baguette with pâté and iced coffee ($4–6), a legacy of French colonial Cambodia
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tuol Sleng at a local Khmer restaurant — try Samlor Machu (sour soup) with rice ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality, serving tapas-style Cambodian street food ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and Tuol Sleng are emotionally demanding — take breaks and process what you see. Photography is permitted but be respectful. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day in Phnom Penh ($15–20). The National Museum closes on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: morning departure from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (or Kep/Kampot for a more relaxed coastal experience). Bus to Kampot takes approximately 3.5 hours ($8–12). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town and the gateway to Kep beach and Rabbit Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot and check into a mid-range guesthouse along the Preaek Tuek Chhu River. Explore Kampot's sleepy French colonial old town — admire the pastel-colored shophouses, visit the old market, and rent a bicycle to explore the riverside at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — drift past mangroves, rice paddies, and the dramatic Bokor Mountain silhouette as the sky turns orange and pink. Stop at a riverside bar for a sundowner with locally-brewed Kampot pepper gin.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure from Phnom Penh
meals.lunch: Lunch at a roadside stop or upon arrival in Kampot — try a Khmer red curry with fresh baguette ($5–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — riverside setting, fresh seafood, and Cambodian dishes ($10–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is known for its famous Kampot pepper — one of the world's finest. Consider buying some as a souvenir. Bicycles and motorbikes can be rented cheaply ($2–5/day) for local exploration. November weather in Kampot is excellent — dry season just beginning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Kep — a former French colonial beach resort town 25 km from Kampot. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and watch fishermen bring in fresh blue crabs. Stroll through Kep National Park's jungle trails with sea views. Visit the haunting ruins of abandoned French villas reclaimed by jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short boat ride from Kep to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, car-free island with white sand beaches, turquoise water, and swaying palm trees. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the beach. Return to Kampot by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a Kampot pepper farm for a guided tour — learn about the cultivation, harvesting, and varieties of Cambodia's prized pepper (red, black, white, and green). Many farms offer evening tours and tasting sessions. End the day with a relaxed riverside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Kampot guesthouse — fresh fruit, yogurt, and Khmer coffee ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on Rabbit Island — freshly grilled fish, squid, and coconut served by beach shack restaurants ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Baraka or Jasmine Valley in Kampot — farm-to-table cuisine featuring local ingredients including Kampot pepper ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boats to Rabbit Island depart from Kep pier and cost approximately $5–7 return. The island has basic beach bungalows if you wish to overnight, but day trips are equally rewarding. Wear reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Pepper farm tours typically cost $3–8 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — wake up early for a sunrise kayak or stand-up paddleboard session on the calm Kampot River. Paddle through mangrove channels and enjoy the peaceful countryside before the day heats up. Return for a leisurely final breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional visit to Bokor National Park (1,075m elevation) — take a tuk-tuk or shared minivan up the winding mountain road to the abandoned French hill station. Explore the eerie ruins of the old Bokor Palace Hotel, a Catholic church, and a casino, all shrouded in mist with sweeping coastal views. Return to Kampot and begin journey back to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap for departure.
day_by_day.evening: If departing from Phnom Penh: arrive by bus in the early evening. Final dinner in Phnom Penh celebrating 10 wonderful days in Cambodia. Pack, rest, and prepare for departure. If departing from Siem Reap, overnight bus or early next-day flight options are available.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — Khmer crepes (Banh Chev) with coconut and banana, fresh fruit, and strong iced coffee ($4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Kampot before departure — sandwich, fresh juice, and Kampot pepper crab spring rolls ($6–9)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — splurge slightly on a final Cambodian feast with amok, lok lak, and fresh coconut dessert ($18–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transport bookings the night before. Phnom Penh International Airport is the main departure hub — allow at least 2.5 hours before international flights. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: Kampot pepper, silk scarves, Angkor-inspired artwork, and Cambodian coffee. Currency tip: spend remaining Cambodian Riel before departure as it is not easily exchanged abroad.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay in Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into the boutique property. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with a dedicated concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimatize. Optional: a rejuvenating arrival spa treatment (60-min Khmer herbal compress massage) to recover from the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle sunset visit to Phnom Bakheng hill temple — a short distance from the Angkor complex — for panoramic golden-hour views over the jungle canopy and distant Angkor Wat silhouette. Return for a private candlelit welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit, Cambodian cold rolls, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant featuring modern Khmer cuisine: amok trey (coconut fish curry in banana leaf), lok lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice dessert, paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport and e-visa are ready for arrival. Pre-arrange a private air-conditioned vehicle for airport transfer. Hydrate well — November in Cambodia is warm and humid even in the dry season. Dress code for Phnom Bakheng: covered shoulders and knees required.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided tour of Angkor Wat for the iconic sunrise. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a prime reflection pool position. A dedicated Angkor scholar-guide will narrate the temple's 12th-century Khmer cosmology, bas-relief galleries depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the five lotus towers. Explore the inner sanctuaries as morning light floods the corridors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Visit the Bayon temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon pyramid temple, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel, served in a shaded pavilion within the complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest period. Head to Siem Reap's Old French Quarter for a private tuk-tuk cultural tour of the night market and artisan quarter. Dinner at a top-tier riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pre-departure early breakfast box from the hotel: fresh croissants, tropical fruit, hard-boiled eggs, yogurt, and thermos of Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet hotel picnic lunch in Angkor Thom: chilled prawn salad, baguette sandwiches with local charcuterie, fresh juices, and petit fours
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or equivalent top Siem Reap fine-dining restaurant — six-course contemporary Cambodian tasting menu with seasonal local ingredients and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise departure requires a 4:45 AM wake-up. Bring insect repellent, a light scarf for temple entry, and comfortable walking shoes. The full Angkor complex can be tiring — pace accordingly and carry water. Book Cuisine Wat Damnak well in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of Ta Prohm — the 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically entwined with giant silk-cotton and strangler fig tree roots. Visit early to beat crowds. Proceed to Preah Khan, a sprawling 12th-century monastic complex with labyrinthine corridors, carved lintels, and a two-story Hellenistic pavilion — a hidden gem of Angkor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for an immersive multimedia journey through Khmer civilization, including the Hall of a Thousand Buddhas and the Gallery of Angkor Kings. Afterward, enjoy a private batik and silk weaving workshop at a local artisan collective, with the option to purchase premium Cambodian silk scarves and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Apsara dance performance — classical Khmer court dance — at a heritage venue, followed by a royal Khmer banquet dinner with traditional music accompaniment.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel: Cambodian rice porridge (bobor) with condiments, eggs benedict, tropical fruit platter, fresh-squeezed juices, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium garden restaurant near the museum: Khmer red curry, grilled Mekong fish, papaya salad, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer banquet dinner — seven-course heritage menu including steamed lotus seed soup, stuffed lemongrass chicken, banana blossom salad, and palm sugar crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded by mid-morning — departing by 7:30 AM is recommended. The Angkor National Museum has a dress code (no sleeveless tops). The Apsara dinner show should be reserved in advance; request a private table for the most immersive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — located 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. This 10th-century pink sandstone temple is considered the jewel of Khmer art, renowned for its extraordinarily intricate carvings of devatas and narrative friezes. Private scholar-guide explains the iconography in depth. En route, stop at Banteay Samré, a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved 12th-century temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (founded by former child soldier Aki Ra) for a sobering and important cultural education on Cambodia's recent history. Continue to a private cooking class at a luxury villa kitchen — learn to prepare three classic Khmer dishes with a celebrated local chef using market-fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the hotel's rooftop bar or pool terrace. Leisurely dinner at the hotel or a selected premium venue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: traditional Cambodian breakfast spread with kuy teav noodle soup, steamed buns, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch en route or at a local family restaurant near Banteay Srei: fresh spring rolls, grilled meats, and Khmer desserts
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant (Siem Reap branch) or equivalent — refined Cambodian cuisine in an elegant open-air setting; signature dishes include stuffed crab and Kampot pepper beef

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a 45-minute drive each way — arrange a comfortable private vehicle. The Landmine Museum is emotionally impactful; it is educational and important but may be distressing for sensitive travelers. Cooking class ingredients can be adjusted for dietary restrictions — inform the chef in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park — a breathtaking aerial perspective of Angkor Wat, the jungle canopy, and the surrounding countryside bathed in golden morning light. (Alternatively, a tethered balloon is available if free flight is weather-restricted.) Return for a leisurely hotel breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Visit the floating villages of Kompong Phluk, where stilted wooden houses rise 6–8 meters above the water. Explore flooded mangrove forests by small wooden boat. Observe daily life of the lake-dwelling communities with a respectful, expert-guided tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset on the lake, returning to Siem Reap by private speedboat. Spa evening at the hotel — choose from a 90-min traditional Khmer massage, a floral bath ritual, or a couples' wellness package. Light dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Post-balloon celebratory breakfast at the hotel: champagne and fresh pastries, full Cambodian and Western breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Lunch on the Tonlé Sap excursion boat — freshly prepared Cambodian lake fish dishes, steamed rice, vegetable stir-fry, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Light and elegant dinner at the hotel's terrace restaurant: Cambodian seafood platter, green mango salad, jasmine rice, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon flights are weather-dependent and may be rescheduled. Book well in advance as spots are limited. The Tonlé Sap lake visit is most spectacular during November when water levels are high post-monsoon. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the boat. Photography is encouraged but always ask permission before photographing local residents.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh by luxury road vehicle (approximately 5–6 hours) or a 45-minute domestic flight (recommended for comfort). Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (e.g., Raffles Hotel Le Royal or Rosewood Phnom Penh). Morning city orientation walk along the riverfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official royal residence featuring stunning Khmer-French architecture, the Throne Hall, and the Silver Pagoda housing a 17th-century Emerald Buddha and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Proceed to the National Museum of Cambodia for an outstanding collection of Khmer sculpture, bronzes, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers (the 'Chaktomuk'). Dinner at a premium Phnom Penh restaurant in the BKK1 or riverside district.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure or en route: fresh baguettes, cheese, cold cuts, and Cambodian iced coffee (Cambodia has a strong French bakery tradition)
meals.lunch: Lunch upon arrival in Phnom Penh at a riverside café: beef lok lak, Cambodian pork and rice, fresh sugar cane juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or equivalent — French-Cambodian fusion fine dining with an extensive wine cellar; signature dishes include foie gras with mango chutney and pan-seared Mekong barramundi

day_by_day.notes: If driving, schedule a comfort stop at Skun or Kampong Cham. Flying is recommended for luxury comfort. The Royal Palace requires conservative dress — long trousers/skirts and covered shoulders mandatory. The Silver Pagoda floor is made of 5,000 silver tiles — shoes must be removed.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. An expert guide provides historical context of the 1975–1979 genocide. Follow with a visit to Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (the Killing Fields), 15 km outside the city, with an award-winning audio guide narration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city for a restorative afternoon. Visit the Psar Thmei (Central Market) — a stunning 1937 Art Deco dome market — for premium shopping: silk, silver jewelry, gemstones, and Cambodian handicrafts. Enjoy a private gemstone consultation at a reputable certified dealer for Cambodian rubies and sapphires.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise on the Mekong aboard a private chartered wooden boat with canapés and champagne. Dinner at a top Phnom Penh establishment.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast: freshly baked croissants, eggs to order, smoked salmon, tropical fruit, Cambodian rice porridge, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a respected social enterprise restaurant (e.g., Friends Restaurant / Romdeng) — supporting former street youth; Cambodian street food elevated to restaurant quality
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma Pasteur or equivalent — sophisticated French brasserie in a colonial villa setting; steak frites, seafood bisque, and crème caramel

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are deeply moving and emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. These sites are essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history and should not be skipped. The private Mekong cruise should be booked in advance. Avoid purchasing gemstones from street vendors — use only certified dealers with provenance documentation.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer or short domestic flight from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (or directly to Koh Rong Samloem island by speedboat). Check in to a luxury beachfront resort on Koh Rong Samloem or Koh Rong — Cambodia's premier island destination with pristine white-sand beaches and turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure on the beach. Snorkeling excursion to nearby coral reefs with a private guide and premium snorkeling equipment. Explore the crystal-clear waters and vibrant marine life. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the magical bioluminescent plankton phenomenon in the bay after dark — the water glows electric blue when disturbed, a truly otherworldly experience. Beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Phnom Penh hotel before departure: continental spread with pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at the resort: grilled fresh catch of the day, coconut rice, tropical salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner at the resort's premium restaurant: whole grilled lobster, prawn skewers, Cambodian seafood curry, and coconut ice cream, with chilled rosé wine

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem takes approximately 45 minutes. Arrange private speedboat transfer for comfort. Bioluminescence is best experienced on moonless nights — check the lunar calendar. November is excellent beach weather in Cambodia (dry season beginning). Bring reef-safe sunscreen only to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered boat tour around the island archipelago — visit secluded beaches, hidden lagoons, and uninhabited islets inaccessible to regular tourists. Snorkeling at a pristine reef site. Optional: beginner scuba diving lesson or guided dive with a certified PADI instructor at a top dive site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious beach afternoon. Enjoy a beachside couples' spa treatment — traditional Khmer massage with coconut oil under a palm-thatched pavilion. Alternatively, take a guided jungle trek through the island's interior to a freshwater stream and natural pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the beach deck with a private bartender crafting signature Cambodian-inspired cocktails (lemongrass mojito, tamarind daiquiri). Final island dinner celebration.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed or on the private terrace: tropical fruit platter, freshly baked pastries, eggs to order, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on a secluded beach during the boat tour: charcuterie board, fresh seafood, artisan bread, tropical fruits, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Farewell island dinner — premium seafood feast: whole steamed crab, tiger prawns, grilled barracuda, fresh oysters, and Cambodian dessert platter with champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: The private boat charter should be arranged through the resort for safety and quality assurance. PADI dive certification courses require advance booking. The jungle trek requires closed-toe shoes and insect repellent. Embrace the slower pace of island life — this is a deliberate luxury detox day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — slow, peaceful breakfast on the beach terrace. One last swim or sunrise walk along the shoreline. Pack and check out of the island resort. Private speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville mainland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if time permits, a brief stop at Otres Beach near Sihanoukville for a final Cambodian beach moment, or a visit to a local artisan market for last-minute premium souvenirs (handwoven baskets, lacquerware, silk). Private luxury vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport or Sihanoukville Airport for onward flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine tropical islands.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the resort: full tropical spread — acai bowls, fresh fruit, eggs benedict, pastries, and celebratory mimosas
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final Cambodian meal at a premium Sihanoukville restaurant: amok trey, grilled prawns, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the departure airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Confirm speedboat and vehicle transfers the evening before. Cambodia's currency is the Riel but USD is widely accepted — settle any remaining bills before departure. Ensure all purchased items (especially gemstones and antiques) have proper documentation for customs. A tip for guides, drivers, and hotel staff is warmly appreciated and culturally appropriate.
